clue.text: Mate taking money into shelter

indicators.note: to take something in is to receive it, so one piece is received inside the other

parts.note: a cote is a small shelter for birds or animals, as in dovecote
the pula is the currency of Botswana

explanation.surface: A friend brings some cash into a refuge for safekeeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mate' reads as a friend, but it is the verb. Botswana's currency is a crossword favourite worth remembering.
explanation.definitionFit: To mate is to pair up sexually, which is exactly what the verb copulate describes in animals or people.

clue.text: Pole in charge of sticky stuff

parts.note: a mast is a tall pole, as on a ship
IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A Polish person is put in charge of some glue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' with its capital letter suggests a Polish person, but it is simply a post.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastic is a resin or putty-like adhesive used as a filler and sealant, so it is literally sticky material.

clue.text: Real centre of democracy on Greek island

indicators.note: a centre is the midpoint of something, so only the letter in the exact middle of the word is kept

parts.note: the fifth of its nine letters
taken as written
Crete is the largest Greek island

explanation.surface: The true birthplace of democracy is supposedly a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to Athens and ancient Greece, but 'centre of democracy' only yields its middle letter, C, followed by ON and CRETE.
explanation.definitionFit: Concrete as an adjective means actual or tangible, existing in physical reality rather than as an abstract idea.

clue.text: Minor embracing exercise is not in good shape

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug and enclose, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: a ward is a minor under the protection of a guardian
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A child who does some exercise still is not fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not in good shape' sounds like being unfit, but it means literally bent out of its proper shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Something warped has been twisted or bent out of its true form, so its physical outline is distorted.

clue.text: Work hard on a new catchphrase

indicators.note: in an across clue, being on something means following it, so the pieces are laid end to end

parts.note: to slog is to toil at a task
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone labours over inventing a fresh catchphrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' looks like it describes the catchphrase, but it only supplies its abbreviation N.
explanation.definitionFit: A slogan is a short memorable phrase used in advertising or politics, the same as a catchphrase.

clue.text: Dish found in scenery outside Globe

indicators.note: being outside something means surrounding it, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a stage set is the scenery for a play
an orb is a globe or sphere

explanation.surface: A plate of food spotted on the stage set outside the Globe theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital G suggests Shakespeare's Globe theatre in London, but it is just a sphere.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorbet is a frozen fruit dessert served as a course, so it counts as a dish on the menu.

clue.text: Composition for soprano working with Australian tenor and alto

parts.note: S is the musical abbreviation for soprano
a machine that is on is working
A is the abbreviation for Australian
T is the musical abbreviation for tenor
A is the musical abbreviation for alto

explanation.surface: A piece written for a soprano performing with an Australian tenor and an alto.
explanation.walkthrough: Every voice part and the nationality shrink to single letters; the musical surface fits the answer perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonata is a musical work, usually in several movements, for one or two instruments, so it is a composition.

clue.text: Setter leaving injured American's treatment for bruises

indicators.note: something injured has been knocked about, so its letters are jumbled
when something is leaving it departs, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: taken as written, the 's being possessive
the setter refers to themself as ME

explanation.surface: The crossword setter walks away from a hurt American, leaving a remedy for their bruising.
explanation.walkthrough: Take ME out of AMERICAN to leave ARICAN, then rearrange those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnica is a herbal preparation from a mountain plant, traditionally rubbed on skin to ease bruising and swelling.

clue.text: Old German revolutionary tucked into dish of fruit

indicators.note: to be tucked into something is to be placed snugly inside it

parts.note: pâté is a savoury paste served as a dish
O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: a revolutionary overturns the order of things, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly German radical is found eating a bowl of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' seems to be a noun describing the German, but it is the anagram signal; 'dish' is a food, not the bowl the fruit sits in.
explanation.definitionFit: A pomegranate is a round tropical fruit with a tough skin packed with juicy red seeds.

clue.text: Heartless publisher to get rid of French author

indicators.note: without a heart, all the inner letters are removed and only the ends remain

parts.note: its first and last letters
to oust is to drive out or get rid of

explanation.surface: A cruel publisher wants to be rid of one of its French writers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' reads as part of 'get rid of', but it links the wordplay to the definition. Marcel Proust wrote In Search of Lost Time.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcel Proust was a celebrated novelist from France, best known for his long work In Search of Lost Time.

clue.text: Oscar trophy found in tin by actor's third tenant

indicators.note: being by something means standing next to it, so the pieces are placed side by side

parts.note: Oscar is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for O

indicators.note: being found in something means sitting inside it

parts.note: a can is a tin container
a cup is a trophy

indicators.note: an ordinal number points to a single letter position within the word

parts.note: the third letter of actor

explanation.surface: An actor's Oscar statuette ends up stored in a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' and 'actor' conjure the Academy Awards, but Oscar is just the phonetic-alphabet letter and the actor supplies one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An occupant is a person living in a property, and a tenant is someone who occupies rented premises.

clue.text: Buffet always includes dairy product

indicators.note: to include is to contain, so the letters are held within the run of words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A buffet spread always has a cheese on it.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across bufFET Always, straddling the gap between words.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a crumbly Greek cheese made from sheep's or goat's milk, and cheese is a milk-based product.

clue.text: Unpleasant character found by retired cops merrymaking in empty clink

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it
an empty word has lost its contents, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: clink is slang for prison; only its first and last letters

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British plain-clothes detectives
to revel is to make merry

explanation.surface: A nasty type is caught alongside some retired policemen partying in an empty jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' governs both the cops and the merrymaking together, so the two pieces are reversed as one string before going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A clever dick is British slang for an irritating know-all who shows off their cleverness, a thoroughly annoying person.

clue.text: Beaten miner agreed with the police

indicators.note: something beaten has been battered out of shape, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A defeated striking miner comes to terms with the police.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the miners' strikes and clashes with police, but 'agreed' is just fodder alongside 'miner'.
explanation.definitionFit: The gendarmerie is a military police force, as in France, so as a body it is a police force.

clue.text: Philosopher stops working to get hold of Socrates' second book

indicators.note: getting hold of something means grasping it, so one piece clasps the other

parts.note: an engine that dies stops working

indicators.note: an ordinal number picks out one letter by its position in the word

parts.note: the second letter of Socrates
Gen is the abbreviation for Genesis, the first book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A philosopher breaks off work to fetch a volume by Socrates.
explanation.walkthrough: Socrates in the surface suggests a second philosopher, but he supplies only one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Diogenes was an ancient Greek thinker, the Cynic said to have lived in a barrel, so he was a philosopher.

clue.text: Difficult universal and timeless tale is deceptive

indicators.note: the suffix -less means without, so the abbreviation for time is removed

parts.note: ill as in ill at ease, awkward or difficult
U is the film classification for universal viewing
a story is a tale; T for time comes out

explanation.surface: A hard, universal, eternal story turns out to be misleading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Timeless' looks like praise for the tale, but it removes T, the abbreviation for time, from STORY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illusory creates a false impression, so it is deceptive in the sense of misleading the senses.

clue.text: Ski lodge in Switzerland rented out after the beginning of April

indicators.note: coming after something places the piece behind it in order

parts.note: CH is Switzerland's international code, from Confoederatio Helvetica

indicators.note: a beginning is where the word starts, so its first letter is taken

parts.note: its first letter
a property let is rented out

explanation.surface: A Swiss ski lodge goes up for rent in early April.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like part of the scene but is the link; Switzerland's code CH starts the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalet is a wooden Alpine house, the typical lodging where skiers stay in mountain resorts.

clue.text: Problems in editions?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: troubles or points of dispute
second meaning: numbers of a magazine or newspaper

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints at the wry idea of misprints plaguing a publication; the two words are separate meanings of one plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural noun covers both matters of concern and the individual numbers published of a periodical.

clue.text: Italian woman cautious about wine

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: chary means wary or cautious
donna is Italian for a lady

explanation.surface: An Italian lady is careful about how much she drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface order puts the inserted piece first; 'about' tells you the second word's synonym wraps around the first's.
explanation.definitionFit: Chardonnay is a white grape variety and the dry white wine made from it.

clue.text: Cloth covering unacceptable stew

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece covering another sits on top of it

parts.note: a rag is a piece of cloth
out as in not allowed or out of the question

explanation.surface: A cloth is thrown over a stew that has gone bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covering' sounds like a lid on the pot, but in a down entry it places RAG above OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragout is a richly seasoned French-style stew of meat and vegetables.

clue.text: Flipping badger eating root of brassica plant

indicators.note: to flip something is to turn it over, so the letters run backwards
whatever eats something takes it inside

parts.note: to badger someone is to worry or pester them

indicators.note: a root is the bottom end of a plant, so the last letter of the word is taken

parts.note: its final letter

explanation.surface: An annoying badger munches a cabbage right down to the root.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badger' is the verb meaning pester, not the animal. WORRY takes in A, and the whole lot is then flipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarrow is a flowering herb with feathery leaves and flat clusters of white flowers, so it is a plant.

clue.text: Juicy drink

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a dated verb, to drink heavily

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a description of fruit juice; the two words are separate meanings, the second a dated verb for drinking alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Lush describes rich succulent growth or fruit, and as an old slang verb means to swill liquor.

clue.text: Bullets containing iron used by tribal leader in hard-fought battle

indicators.note: one thing used by another is set right beside it, so the pieces are joined
to contain something is to hold it inside

parts.note: slugs are bullets
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: a leader goes at the front, so the first letter is taken

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: Iron bullets fired by a tribal chief in a fierce fight.
explanation.walkthrough: SLUGS holds FE, then T joins the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A slugfest is a fight or contest marked by heavy blows traded back and forth, a bruising battle.

clue.text: Save soldiers with special signal

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
S is the abbreviation for special
a cue is a signal to begin

explanation.surface: Troops carry out a rescue using a secret signal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' reads as joining soldiers to signal, but it links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescue someone is to save them from danger or harm, the verb in its usual sense.

clue.text: Pout about extremely expensive hair product

indicators.note: about can mean turned around or out of order, so the letters are moved

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone sulks about the steep price of a hair treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning', but it rearranges POUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A toupee is a small hairpiece worn to cover a bald patch, a manufactured item for the hair.

clue.text: Crafty poet married Iris

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for married
orris is a type of iris grown for its fragrant root

explanation.surface: A cunning poet wed a woman named Iris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crafty' suggests sly, but William Morris led the Arts and Crafts movement, and 'Iris' is the flower, not a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: William Morris was a Victorian poet and a founder of the Arts and Crafts design movement, hence crafty.
